llm.summary: The skill is coherent with its stated purpose (a file-based retrieval+compression pipeline) but its runtime contract requires reading and pasting workspace memory files (potentially sensitive) into transcripts and modifying repo files without declaring runtime binaries — this warrants caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, router, schemas, prompts, and included scripts all align with a file-based retrieval + compression pipeline. The skill requires no external credentials and uses only workspace files. Minor mismatch: the package includes Python scripts and expects git operations, but the registry metadata lists no required binaries — the skill implicitly requires a Python runtime and git available in the environment.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md mandates the agent run installer/validator/watchdog scripts, patch AGENTS.md, and — importantly — emit complete artifacts (Retrieval Bundle JSON and Context Pack JSON) and raw snippet content into the transcript. Emitting snippet text (workspace memory files) into the agent transcript can expose sensitive or secret data. The instructions also require the agent to modify repository files (AGENTS.md) and paste git diffs, which grants write access to the user's workspace; this is coherent with the skill's purpose but increases the risk surface.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external install spec is present (instruction-only at registry level) and included scripts operate on bundled assets via local copy. All code is packaged with the skill; there are no downloads from arbitrary URLs or use of external release hosts. The installer copies files from the skill's assets into the workspace and computes local hashes — expected and low risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no credentials or env vars, which is appropriate. However, its runtime contract requires reading the workspace memory/ directory and pasting retrieved snippet contents into transcripts. That means any secrets or private information stored in memory files would be surfaced to the agent (and possibly to external LLM providers). The number of env/config requests is low, but file read/write scope is broad relative to a simple helper — review memory contents before enabling.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always:true' and does not declare elevated platform privileges. It does instruct the agent to install files into the user's workspace and to edit AGENTS.md, which is normal for an installable pipeline but does require write access to the repo. Autonomous invocation is allowed (default) — combine that with the above data-access concerns when evaluating risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement the described retrieval+compression pipeline and includes local installer/validator/watchdog scripts. Before installing, review these points:

- Review memory files first: The skill requires reading your workspace memory (memory/always_on.md, memory/topics/, daily logs) and will paste snippet text into transcripts. Remove or redact any secrets or sensitive material from those files before enabling.
- Execution environment: The scripts are Python; ensure python3 and git are available and accept that the skill will write files into your workspace (context_pipeline/) and modify AGENTS.md when you 'apply' it. Back up AGENTS.md first.
- Transcript exposure: The runtime contract explicitly requires emitting Retrieval Bundle and Context Pack JSON and snippet text into the agent transcript. If your agent uses external LLM endpoints, this will send that data outside your local environment. If you cannot tolerate that, do not enable it or run it offline/local only.
- Test in a safe workspace: Try the installer and validator in a throwaway repo to observe outputs and behavior before applying to production content.
- If you need a tighter fit: request a version that limits pasted snippet text, or update the runtime checklist to redact or summarize sensitive fields before emitting them.

Confidence is medium: the skill is internally coherent with its purpose but the mandatory evidence-emission and file-write steps create a non-trivial data-exposure risk that users should consider.
